title: Maximum Number of Operations to Move Ones to the End
summary: Given a binary string, you can repeatedly move '1's to the right by one position to the end of the string, provided the next character is '0'.
statement: Given a binary string, you can repeatedly move '1's to the right by one position to the end of the string, provided the next character is '0'. The task is to determine the maximum number of such operations possible.
constraints: s is a nonempty binary string.
One operation chooses a 1 immediately followed by 0 and moves that 1 right across the entire consecutive zero block.
Return the maximum number of operations possible under an optimal order.
hints: At the start of a zero block, every one seen earlier can eventually be moved across that block once.
Count prefix ones and add that count only on a 1-to-0 boundary.
Increment ones on 1; on 0 with previous 1 add ones.
Each operation can be charged uniquely to a one and a later zero block, and processing blocks left to right realizes every such charge.
editorial: Each operation can be charged uniquely to a one and a later zero block, and processing blocks left to right realizes every such charge.

tests.explanation: The first zero block can receive one earlier one and the later zero block can receive three, totaling four operations.
No one has a zero block to its right, so no operation is possible.
